start.title: Start here
start.html:
Welcome to Kiitos. You're about to have your own testimonial engine, running in your own account, that you never pay a monthly fee for.

What you'll have by the end

  • A friendly form you can send to clients today
  • A Wall of Love page you can link from anywhere
  • Testimonials scrolling on your own website

How long it takes

About half an hour for the Set up Kiitos and Collect and share lessons. Everything after that can wait for another day.

What you need

  1. An email address
  2. A free Netlify account. Netlify is the home your Kiitos lives in.
  3. A free GitHub account. GitHub keeps your copy of Kiitos safe, a bit like a filing cabinet you never have to open.

You don't need to write any code, and you don't need to understand Netlify or GitHub. You click, you choose a password, you're in. Every lesson shows you exactly where to click, with a short moving picture of each step.

What it costs to run

Kiitos lives in your own Netlify account, with nothing else to subscribe to. A free Netlify account comes with monthly credits. The AI helpers and updates use a few of them, and a full AI report costs pennies.

One promise

Your testimonials are yours. They sit in your account, and you can download every one of them whenever you like.

Updates are included too. When a new version is ready, your Kiitos tells you, and the Getting updates lesson shows you how to get it in about two minutes.

Ready? Head to Get your own copy of Kiitos.

copy.title: Get your own copy of Kiitos
copy.html:
By the end of this lesson Kiitos is copied into your own accounts and Netlify is putting it online.

  1. Click this button, Deploy Kiitos to Netlify. It opens in a new tab.
  2. Sign in to Netlify, or create a free account if you're new.
  3. Netlify asks to connect to GitHub. Sign in there too, or create a free account. This is where your copy of Kiitos is kept.
  4. Netlify asks for one thing, called ADMIN_PASSWORD. This is the password you'll use to log in to Kiitos. Choose a good one and save it in your password manager now.
  5. Click the button to deploy, and let Netlify work. It takes a minute or two.

You're done when Netlify shows your new site with an address that ends in netlify.app. Copy that address somewhere handy. That's your Kiitos.

About your GitHub copy

Netlify has put a copy of Kiitos in your GitHub account. You never need to open it, and it's best left exactly as it is. Updates reach you through Netlify, not GitHub.

Something went wrong? Take a screenshot before you close anything, then see the Getting help lesson.

login.title: Log in for the first time
login.html:
By the end of this lesson you're inside your Kiitos admin, looking at your Inbox.

  1. Take your site address from the last lesson and add /admin to the end, like your-site.netlify.app/admin
  2. Type the password you chose.
  3. Bookmark the page so you can always find it.
[[GIF:lesson-2a-log-in.gif]]

You stay logged in on each device for two weeks.

Good to know. Five wrong passwords in a row lock the login for 15 minutes. Make a cup of tea and try again.

Have a look around

The side panel on the left has four groups.

  • Collect holds Forms and Import
  • Manage holds your Inbox
  • Share holds Walls of Love and Widgets
  • Analyse holds Voice of Customer
[[GIF:lesson-2b-look-around.gif]]

At the bottom you'll find Guide, which explains every screen in plain English. It's always there when you forget something.

look.title: Make it look like you
look.html:
By the end of this lesson every form, wall and widget carries your name, your colours and your fonts.

Open Settings at the bottom of the side panel.

  1. Brand. Fill in your brand name, your first name, what you do and your website. Your first name and what you do also help the AI helpers write about your work properly.
  2. Style. Tap one of the five ready-made looks, Neutral, Editorial, Soft and warm, Colourful, or Bold and playful. Each one fills in all the colours and fonts for you.
[[GIF:lesson-3a-brand-and-style.gif]]
  1. Preview. Flick through the four tabs, Wall of Love, Form, Widgets and Share card. You're looking at your real pages with your choices on them.
[[GIF:lesson-3b-preview.gif]]
  1. Colours and fonts. Tweak anything you like. Colours are codes like #FAED23. Fonts are names from Google Fonts, spelt exactly as Google spells them.
  2. Tap Save settings.
[[GIF:lesson-3c-save-settings.gif]]

Nothing changes for your clients until you save, so play as much as you like first.

Consent wording sits at the bottom of Settings. These are the questions people answer on the last screen of each form, about showing their name and their photo. The starter wording works as it is.

form.title: Your first form
form.html:
By the end of this lesson you have a link you can send to a client, and you've watched a testimonial arrive.

Open Forms in the side panel. Kiitos comes with a starter form.

  1. Tap Edit on the starter form.
  2. Change the title and the welcome words so they sound like you.
  3. Rewrite the questions. Two or three is plenty. Questions like "What changed for you?" get better answers than "Any feedback?"
  4. Decide whether to ask for a star rating.
  5. Check the tags. Every testimonial sent through this form picks up these tags, and tags are how testimonials find their way onto the right wall.
  6. Tap Save changes.
[[GIF:lesson-4a-edit-your-form.gif]]

Now test it

The preview at the bottom of the form is real. Send yourself a testimonial from it.

[[GIF:lesson-4c-send-a-test.gif]]

Then open your Inbox. There it is, marked Waiting. Tap Approve.

[[GIF:lesson-4d-approve.gif]]

Send it to a real person

Back in Forms, tap Copy link and paste it into a WhatsApp message or an email.

[[GIF:lesson-4b-copy-your-link.gif]]

A nice touch. Add ?name= and their name to the end of the link, and the form greets them with their name already filled in.

Running more than one programme? Tap Duplicate on a form, change the title, questions and tags, then save. One form per programme keeps everything sorted without any effort from you.

wall.title: Your first Wall of Love
wall.html:
By the end of this lesson you have a public page of testimonials you can link from your website, your bio or a sales email.

Open Walls of Love in the side panel. Kiitos comes with a starter wall.

A wall is a group of approved testimonials, chosen by tag. A wall with no tags at all shows every approved testimonial, which makes a lovely everything page.

  1. Tap Edit on your wall and find Wall words. Change the small label, the headline and the line underneath, then tap Save changes.
[[GIF:lesson-5a-wall-words.gif]]
  1. Choose its tags. Any of these tags means a testimonial needs just one of them. All of these tags means it needs every one.
  2. Tap Copy link and open it in a new tab. Your test testimonial from the last lesson should be on it.
[[GIF:lesson-5b-see-your-wall.gif]]

Fine-tuning, for later

  • Pin keeps a testimonial on this wall whatever its tags.
  • Leave off removes it from this wall only.
  • The Order menu changes the order. Pick My own order to arrange them by hand with the arrows.
  • Marking a testimonial Featured (in the Inbox, under Edit) shows it first.

About names and photos

If someone said no to showing their name, the wall shows their initials. If they said no to their photo, it stays private. You can't override that, and that's on purpose.

Tidy up. Go back to the Inbox and tap Hide on your test testimonial.

widgets.title: Put testimonials on your website
widgets.html:
By the end of this lesson your testimonials are showing on your own website, and they keep themselves up to date from now on.

Open Widgets in the side panel.

  1. Pick a collection. That's Kiitos's word for a wall here.
  2. Pick a style. There are scrolling rows, an avatar strip, a rating badge, a grid and a single card.
  3. Tweak it and watch the preview.
[[GIF:lesson-6a-widgets-a.gif]]
  1. Tap Copy embed code.
[[GIF:lesson-6a-widgets-b.gif]]
  1. In your website builder, add an Embed Code or HTML element, paste the code in and publish.

Two tips for any website builder

  • Stretch the element to the full width of the page.
  • If your builder asks for a height, use the number the Widgets screen shows you.

Some builders show the widget as a blank box while you're editing. That's normal. It comes to life on the published page.

You never need to touch your website again to update a widget. Approve, hide or edit a testimonial in Kiitos and every widget follows.

alerts.title: Get an email when a testimonial arrives
alerts.html:
By the end of this lesson every new testimonial sends you an email. This one is optional. Your Inbox catches everything either way.

The emails come from Netlify, so this lesson happens over there.

  1. Log in to Netlify and click your Kiitos site.
  2. Go to Forms and tap Enable form detection.
  3. Go to Deploys, then Trigger deploy, then Deploy project. This puts your site live again with the change, and takes a minute or two.
  4. Back in Forms, find Form notifications and add an email notification for the form called new-testimonial. Type the address you want alerts sent to.

Test it

Send yourself a testimonial from a form preview. The email shows their name, the programme, their stars, the first few lines and a link straight to it in your admin.

No email? Check your spam folder first. Then look at Netlify's Forms screen, which keeps a list of every alert it sent.

Alerts never include the person's email address, and a missed alert never loses a testimonial.

ai.title: Meet your AI helpers
ai.html:
By the end of this lesson you've pulled the best line out of a testimonial and seen what your clients talk about most.

There's nothing to switch on and no key to paste. The helpers run on Netlify's built-in AI and use your Netlify credits. A full run over all your testimonials costs pennies. To see your credits, go to Netlify, then Usage & billing.

These get more useful the more testimonials you have, so come back to this lesson once a few have landed. Already have testimonials somewhere else? Import in the side panel brings them in from a screenshot, a spreadsheet or by hand.

Suggest highlights

A highlight is the one sentence that shows in the scrolling rows and on share cards. In the Inbox, tap Suggest highlights. The AI picks the best lines, word for word, and you tap the one you like. Nothing changes until you tap.

Themes

In the Inbox, tap Find my themes. The AI reads everything and names what people talk about most. Tap a theme to see just those testimonials. Themes are only for you. They never show on your walls or widgets.

Voice of Customer

Find it in the side panel under Analyse. Choose who the report covers, then tap a report like Life before you or Words they use, or type your own question under Ask anything. Every point comes with real quotes, checked word for word against what your clients wrote. Tap Copy and you have the raw material for a sales page, an email or a caption.

Share cards

Tap Share card on any approved testimonial. Pick square, tall or Story, pick a background from your brand colours, and save the image for Instagram.

care.title: Looking after your Kiitos
care.html:
Your week in two minutes

New testimonials land in the Inbox marked Waiting. Tap Approve on the good ones and Hide on anything you don't want to use. Your walls and widgets update by themselves. Hid the wrong one? Tap Undo in the little pop-up.

[[GIF:lesson-9a-hide-and-undo.gif]]

Back up once a month

Open Import, tap Backups, then use Download JSON for a full backup of everything, or Download CSV for a file that opens in Excel or Google Sheets.

[[GIF:lesson-9b-back-up.gif]]

Changing your password

In Netlify, go to Environment variables, change ADMIN_PASSWORD, then go to Deploys, Trigger deploy, Deploy project. Every device gets logged out and you log in again with the new one.

Hide or delete?

Hide is always safe and always undoable. If you need a testimonial gone completely, hide it and save, then open it again and use Delete for good at the bottom. That one can't be undone.

One thing to leave alone

Netlify has a screen called Blobs with bin icons. Those delete things for good. Do your tidying from the Kiitos admin instead.

updates.title: Getting updates
updates.html:
By the end of this lesson you know how to tell when a new version of Kiitos is ready, how to get it, and how to check it worked.

Every update is included with Kiitos. Nothing happens to your copy without you, because each update uses a few of your Netlify credits and you get to choose when to spend them.

How you'll know there's an update

A note appears at the top of your Inbox, saying something like "Kiitos 0.3.0 is ready (you're on 0.2.0)". Kiitos checks for news about twice a day, so you might see it a few hours after a new version comes out.

The note has two buttons.

  • See what's new opens a short list of what changed.
  • How to update opens the Updates part of your Guide, with the same steps as this lesson.

You can check which version you're on at any time. Open Guide in the side panel and look at the line at the top.

How to update

  1. Log in to Netlify and click your Kiitos site.
  2. Click Deploys.
  3. Click Trigger deploy, then Deploy project.
  4. Wait a minute or two. The newest deploy appears at the top of the list, and you're done when it says Published.

Then go back to your admin and refresh the page. The note in your Inbox has gone, and the Guide shows your new version number.

What stays exactly the same

Your testimonials, forms, walls, widgets, settings, colours and fonts. They're stored separately from the app, so an update never touches them. The widgets on your website keep working without you changing anything there.

Good to know

  • No rush. Your Kiitos keeps working on the version it has for as long as you like.
  • Skipped a few? One update brings you straight to the newest version.
  • Want proof it worked? In Netlify, click the newest deploy and look through its log for a line that starts with [Kiitos update]. It tells you which version you moved to.
  • If an update can't be fetched, nothing breaks. Kiitos carries on with the version you already have, and you can try again later.
  • Leave your GitHub copy alone. If you or a developer ever change the code there, the next update replaces those changes.

help.title: Getting help
help.html:
Stuck? Start with the Guide. It's at the bottom of the side panel in your admin, and it explains every screen in plain English.

Still stuck? Email Dan at dannybunny@mac.com and include three things.

  1. A screenshot of what you're seeing
  2. Which screen you were on
  3. What you tapped just before it went wrong

That's usually enough to sort it in one reply.
